rationale: Evidence from the last race (iteration 2, score 625.2): the oval finished 20/20 at 2.06 s, the s-bend finished 15/20 (5 off-track), and the slalom finished 0/20, every failure off_track at progress about 0.36. max_error sits near the 0.06 m off-track limit on the failing tracks. Steering oscillation is moderate (0.17 oval, 0.35 s-bend, 0.26 slalom) and control effort is high on the slalom (10.7), so the robot is correcting hard and still lagging through bends. The forward move from y=0.05 to y=0.07 helped (score 185 to 625), which suggests more sensing lead still pays off. Changes: (1) sensor y 0.07 -> 0.08, the maximum allowed, for the most lead time on bends. (2) kd 0.8 -> 1.0 to damp the faster corrections the extra lead produces. (3) base_speed 1.2 -> 1.1 so the robot has more steering margin on tight bends. The oval (2.06 s at 1.2) should still finish near 2.25 s and the s-bend near 2.6 s, both under 3 s. kp 4.5, ki 0.02, sensor x spread, weights, geometry and line_loss are unchanged so the effect of these three changes is isolated. Expected result: slalom completions begin to appear and s-bend finishes rise toward 18-20/20, with steering_oscillation staying below about 0.4. Risk: base_speed 1.1 costs time on the oval and s-bend, and if kd 1.0 causes sluggish correction the slalom may still leave the line. Hypotheses for next iteration: if the slalom still exits at low progress, the bottleneck is steering authority and kp should rise to about 5; if oscillation exceeds 0.4, kd is too high; if completion_time on the oval exceeds 2.5 s, base_speed should go back to about 1.2. Measurements requested: completion, progress and completion_time for the speed trade-off, max_error and line_loss_events for recovery, and steering_oscillation and control_effort for gain stability.
